**Visual Analysis of the Test Image:**

- **Affected part**: Banana leaf
- **Key features observed**:
  - Multiple dark brown to black spots scattered across the leaf surface
  - Spots have lighter grey/tan centers with darker brown/black borders
  - Distinct yellow halos surrounding several spots
  - Yellow/brown discoloration along the leaf margin, especially where spots are coalescing
  - Spots are distributed across the full leaf blade, more densely near the margin

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Matches very well — "small, dark brown to black spots on banana leaves that enlarge and coalesce, causing leaves to turn yellow." The image shows exactly this: dark spots with yellow halos and marginal yellowing where spots are coalescing.
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Possible, but the description in the knowledge base (under Phyllosticta_Maculata) describes diamond-shaped brown spots with yellow margins at right angles to leaf length — the spots here are more rounded/oval and scattered.
- **Panama_Disease**: Causes wilting/death of whole plant — no match.
- **Anthracnose**: Fruit disease — no match.
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: Fruit disease — no match.
- **Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus / Bunchy_Top**: Causes stunted erect leaves with marginal chlorosis — no spot pattern match.

The pattern of dark brown/black spots with yellow halos and leaf margin yellowing/coalescence is a textbook presentation of Yellow and Black Sigatoka on banana leaves.
